initialContact.message: I'm 48 and starting to seriously think about retirement. I have good työeläke from my employer, but I'm wondering if I should save more. My bank is pushing 'vapaaehtoinen eläkesäästäminen' (voluntary pension savings) - they say it's tax-deductible up to 5,000€/year and grows tax-free. But I could also just invest in index funds myself with more flexibility. What's actually better? The pension product sounds good but locks money until retirement.

problemContext.currentSituation: Accountant with good pension planning additional retirement savings, comparing voluntary pension products vs regular investing

idealAdvice: Great that you're planning ahead - 48 is perfect time to boost retirement savings
Voluntary pension savings (TyEL-lisä, PS-tili) pros: tax deduction (25% of contribution), tax-free growth, forced discipline
Cons: Money locked until retirement (usually 68), limited investment options, fees can be high
Regular index fund investing pros: complete flexibility, lower fees, can access anytime, more investment options
Cons: No tax deduction on contribution, capital gains tax when selling (30-34%)
You likely already have solid työeläke - supplemental savings is smart but not desperate need
Hybrid approach often best: Use voluntary pension for tax deduction (maybe 3-5k/year), plus index funds for flexibility
Tax benefit: If you're in ~30% tax bracket, 5,000€ contribution costs you ~3,500€ after deduction
BUT: Weigh against losing liquidity for 20 years. Can you afford to lock money away?
With 32k€ in savings and good income - yes, you can afford to lock some away
Consider: 3,000€/year to voluntary pension (tax benefit), 3,000€/year to index funds (flexibility)
Review fees carefully - some voluntary pension products have 1-2% annual fees which erode returns
commonMistakes: Pushing voluntary pension without explaining downsides (liquidity lock)
Dismissing voluntary pension without acknowledging tax benefits
Not suggesting hybrid approach combining both strategies
Failing to account for her specific financial situation (already secure)
Forgetting she's an accountant who appreciates detailed analysis
